# Security Architecture Guidance

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../../README.md) • [Strategy](../../README.md) • [Guidance](../README.md)**

---

This folder contains the enterprise **Security Architecture Guidance** set for Gainwell Technologies. It provides TOGAF-aligned capability models, Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs), and Reference Architecture Documents (RADs) across all security capability domains.

---
page_texts.2:
[strategy/guidance/security/README.md#what-this-is]

## What This Is

Security Architecture Guidance defines the **what** and the **how** of security architecture at the enterprise level:

- **Capability maps** — what security capabilities the enterprise must possess
- **ABBs** — reusable architectural building blocks that describe components and their required behaviors
- **Reference architecture documents** — illustrative patterns showing how ABBs compose into deployed solutions

This content is **normative on architectural intent** and **illustrative on implementation**. It does not mandate specific products or configurations.

[strategy/guidance/security/README.md#what-this-is-not]

## What This Is NOT

| Not in scope here | Where to find it |
|---|---|
| Security controls, configuration baselines, and enforceable standards | `standards/security/` |
| Technology-specific deployment configuration | `standards/security/` or component-level runbooks |
| Security policy (regulatory/legal/governance obligations) | `governance/` |
| Security operations procedures and incident response | `strategy/guidance/security/SecOps/` |
| Architecture decision records | `decisions/security/` |

page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/README.md#three-tier-content-model]

## Three-Tier Content Model

All security guidance is structured in three tiers following TOGAF Architecture Content Framework:

| Tier | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **L1 / L2** | Capability Maps and Descriptions | Define what the enterprise must be able to do; model capabilities at the domain and sub-domain level |
| **L3** | Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs) | Define the architectural components that realize each capability; prescribe behaviors using SHALL/SHOULD/MAY |
| **L3** | Reference Architecture Documents (RADs) | Illustrate how ABBs compose into deployed logical architectures; provide patterns for platform and solution teams |

Architects begin with the Capability Map to understand scope, then review ABBs for architectural requirements, then consult RADs for implementation patterns.

[strategy/guidance/security/README.md#how-to-use-this-guidance]

## How to Use This Guidance

1. **Identify the relevant capability domain** using the table above
2. **Read the Capability Vision document** for that domain (the `REF-1.x.01` file in each domain folder)
3. **Review the Capability Map** (L1/L2 documents) to understand scope and sub-capabilities
4. **Consult the ABB Catalog** to identify which building blocks are required for your solution context
5. **Read the relevant ABB definitions** to understand architectural requirements (SHALL/SHOULD/MAY)
6. **Use the Reference Architecture Documents** as illustrative patterns for logical design

---
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/README.md#how-to-contribute]

## How to Contribute

New security guidance content must follow the three-tier model and authoring templates in `resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/`. Before creating content:

1. Review the existing capability domain folder to understand what already exists
2. Ensure naming convention compliance: `GUID-SEC-<DOMAIN>-<TYPE>-<LEVEL>.<DOMAIN>.<SEQ>.md`
3. Use the appropriate template from `resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/`
4. Link new ABBs to their parent ABB Catalog and Capability Vision documents
5. Update the domain's `README.md` to index new documents
6. Create or update a Reference Architecture Document when multiple ABBs compose into a pattern

Raise an ADO work item tagged `Security` and `architecture-review` before beginning work on a new domain or major revision.
